stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In 2019, paleobotanist Ines Kovač published a description of fossil leaves from a limestone quarry near Labin, Croatia, identifying them as a previously unknown species of seed fern. Her analysis rested on the branching pattern of the leaves' veins, which differs from that of true ferns. ______ a geology student had collected nearly identical leaves at the same quarry in 1987, but he labeled them as ordinary ferns, and the specimens sat unexamined in a museum drawer for three decades.
explanation: Put a date on each sentence. Kovač's description is from 2019. The blank sentence is about 1987. The sentence after the blank goes back 32 years to give background on an earlier find, so you need a word that points backward. "Previously" does that.

A.why: You assumed the passage keeps moving forward because the 1987 sentence comes second. Compare the dates: 1987 is before 2019, so "subsequently" points the wrong way in time.

C.why: You read the order of the sentences as cause and effect. Kovač's 2019 study could not have caused a student to collect leaves in 1987.

D.why: You saw that both sentences involve similar leaves and went for a similarity word. The blank sentence isn't offering a parallel case. It moves back in time to explain what happened earlier at the quarry.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Hailstones form in three stages inside a thunderstorm. First, supercooled water droplets freeze onto a speck of dust or pollen, creating a small ice pellet called an embryo. Strong updrafts then carry the embryo up and down through the cloud many times, and each trip adds a new layer of ice. ______ the stone becomes too heavy for the updraft to hold aloft, and it falls to the ground as hail.
explanation: The passage promises three stages and marks them with "first" and "then." The blank sentence describes the last stage, the moment the stone falls after many trips through the cloud. "Eventually" marks that final step in the process.

A.why: You put the blank sentence earlier in the timeline than it is. The stone falls only after the layering stage, so a backward-pointing word reverses the order of the steps.

B.why: You read the falling stone as one example of the layering process. It is the next and last stage, not a sample of the one before it.

D.why: You mistook a change in what happens (the stone stops rising) for a contradiction. The sentence finishes the sequence. It doesn't disagree with anything said before it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In 1974, after months of protests from residents who objected to losing access to the river, the Ashford city council halted construction of a six-lane expressway along the waterfront. The cleared land was later turned into Millrace Park, now the city's largest public green space. ______ consultant Harold Breck had recommended the riverfront route in 1958, arguing that the riverbank was the only corridor in Ashford wide enough to hold the highway.
explanation: The passage starts in 1974 and then mentions the park that came later. The blank sentence goes back to 1958, when Breck first proposed the route, and "had recommended" confirms the step back. "Earlier" marks that move into the past to give background.

A.why: You followed the order of the sentences rather than the dates. Breck's 1958 recommendation came 16 years before the 1974 halt, not after it.

C.why: You treated one event following another as cause and effect. The council's 1974 decision and the park didn't lead to a recommendation made in 1958.

D.why: You treated the blank sentence as one more fact added to the story. It does more than that: it goes back in time to explain where the expressway plan began, so you need a time word.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: To keep the aging Halvorsen Dam from sliding under the pressure of its reservoir, engineers began a reinforcement project in 2008. Crews drilled vertical shafts through the dam's concrete and threaded steel cables deep into the bedrock below. The cables were tightened gradually, a few at a time, so the structure could adjust to each new load. ______ in 2012, the last cable was locked in place, and the dam's resistance to sliding had nearly doubled.
explanation: Line up the times: the project begins in 2008, the cables are tightened one group after another, and the blank sentence is set in 2012, when the last cable goes in. That is the closing step of the procedure, so "finally" is the right word.

A.why: You chose a backward time word without checking the dates. 2012 is after the 2008 start and after the gradual tightening, so the sentence moves forward, not back.

B.why: You read the 2012 sentence as a sample of the tightening process. It reports the end of the project, not one example of a step.

C.why: You expected a contrast. Locking the last cable and doubling the dam's resistance is what the project was designed to do, so nothing is being contradicted.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Economist Ruth Adeyemi's history of the Dalton textile mills traces two systems the mills used to pay their workers. In the 1890s, most mill hands earned a piece rate: they were paid for each yard of cloth they wove, so faster weavers took home more. ______ the mills replaced piece rates with a fixed hourly wage in 1923, after new automated looms made it nearly impossible to measure any one worker's output.
explanation: The passage names two pay systems. The sentence before the blank sets the first one in the 1890s, and the blank sentence moves to 1923, when the second one began. That is a jump forward of about three decades, so "Decades later" fits.

A.why: You flipped the timeline. The 1923 hourly wage came after the piece rates of the 1890s, so a backward-pointing word gets the order wrong.

B.why: You saw that the first sentence names a category ("two systems") and assumed the blank brings in one example. The piece rate was already the first system. The blank sentence moves forward in time to the second.

D.why: You treated the two pay systems as alike. An hourly wage replaced pay by the yard, so the second system is a change, not a parallel.
